import pytest

def test_will_it_fly():
    # Object is palindromic and light enough -> flies
    assert will_it_fly([3, 2, 3], 9) == True
    assert will_it_fly([3, 2, 3], 8) == False  # too heavy
    assert will_it_fly([3], 5) == True          # single element, light
    assert will_it_fly([3], 2) == False         # single element, too heavy
    assert will_it_fly([1, 2], 5) == False      # not palindromic
    assert will_it_fly([1, 2, 1, 2], 10) == False  # not palindromic
    assert will_it_fly([1, 2, 2, 1], 6) == True    # palindrome, exact weight
    assert will_it_fly([5], 5) == True             # exact weight boundary
    assert will_it_fly([], 0) == True              # empty list flies
    assert will_it_fly([], 1) == True              # empty list flies
    assert will_it_fly([1, 2, 3, 2, 1], 100) == True   # odd-length palindrome
    assert will_it_fly([4, 4], 8) == True              # even-length palindrome
    assert will_it_fly([1, 2, 3], 6) == False          # not palindrome
    assert will_it_fly([0, 0], 0) == True              # zeros, exact weight
    assert will_it_fly([7, 7, 7], 20) == False         # sum exceeds weight
